lines.li: [them,task:you] You write a good letter, and often.
[them,!task:you] {OFFICER} writes to us so often that we know the messenger by name.
[us,task:you] I like to think someone reads them.
[us,!task:you] {OFFICER} enjoys it more than we do the chores, I think.
[them] They're read, all of them.
[us] How does your head find us these days?
[them,their:tribal] The elders speak of your camp more kindly than they did.
[them,their:empire] Your name is mentioned at court without a frown now, which is something.
[them] Better than last year, I'd say.
[us] Good, we mean to keep it that way.
[them,task:you] You came to see us not long ago, didn't you?
[them,!task:you] {OFFICER} came to see us not long ago, and people still talk about it.
[us,task:you] I was, and I ate better there than I do here.
[us,!task:you] {OFFICER} came back with more stories than luggage.
[them] Come again, then.
[them] Your {OFFICE} keeps asking our traders what we're short of.
[us] {OFFICER} counts everything, it's a habit.
[them,their:tribal] Our hunters say your goods are good, which they don't say often.
[them] If the prices are fair, our caravans could stop here more often.
[us] What would sell well where you come from, do you think?
[them,their:spacer] Anything that still works after a season in the dust.
[them] Anything you can spare that we can't make ourselves.
[them] Your {OFFICE} wrote to us about our people in your cells.
[us] They're fed and kept warm, whatever else you've heard.
[them] Their families want them home.
[us] Then make an offer, and we'll hear it.
[us] You know we want our own back.
[them] Your {OFFICE} has made that very clear in writing.
[us] Then you know we're willing to talk about a price.
[them] Your {OFFICE} writes to our head about the faith, I'm told.
[us] It's good to have neighbors who pray the same way.
[them,their:lowtech] We said your names at the last rite, as you say ours.
[them] It is, these days especially.
[them] Your {OFFICE} has been writing to our head about your faith.
[us] {OFFICER} believes it, and believes in saying so.
[them] Our head reads every letter, and argues with half of them out loud.
[us] That's more than most do.
[them] Does {OFFICER} ever write about anything but faith?
[us] Not often, no.
[them] I hear there's to be a feast, and our people are asked.
[us,task:you] There is, and I mean it to be a good one.
[us,!task:you] {OFFICER} is already worrying about the seating.
[them,their:tribal] We will bring meat, as guests should.
[them] We'll come hungry, then.
[them] Your {OFFICE} means to come and drill our fighters, I hear.
[us] {OFFICER} drills ours until they drop, so be warned.
[them,their:tribal] Our hunters will want to see if your ways are better than ours.
[them] Good, some of ours could use it.
[them] They say your {OFFICE} will come to our sick with medicine.
[us] {OFFICER} wants to, if the road allows it.
[them] Tell {OFFICER} to come soon, there are a lot of them.
[them] I know what you were asking about, last time.
[us] I ask a lot of people a lot of things.
[them] Not about me, not again.
[them] Your keeper of secrets should mind their own business.
[us] I'll pass that on.
[us] You seem careful with what you say around here.
[them,their:empire] At court we learn to be, and here it seems the same.
[them] I've learned to be, in this colony.
[us] Fair enough.
[them] I haven't forgotten your colony's letter.
[us] Nobody asked you to.
[them] Remember that I haven't, then.
[them] Neighbors who deal in other people's shame are no neighbors.
[us] You had a choice.
[them] Someone of yours walked behind us half the night.
[us] Just making sure you had what you needed.
[them,their:empire] At court that is called a spy, and not politely.
[them] Is that what it was?
[them] Your people keep late hours: someone sat up with us till the fire burned low.
[us] We don't get guests every night, so we make the most of them.
[them] Last time we talked trade, and now your {OFFICE} writes to us about it.
[us] We took you at your word.
[them] Good, so did we.
[them] {THEN} is still with us, you know.
[us] That's why our {OFFICE} means to come with medicine.
[them] Then we'll be watching the road.
[us] You told me about {THEN} last time, does {THEN} read our letters?
[them] Every one, and out loud at supper.
[us] Then we'll keep them short.
[them] Your {OFFICE} keeps busy, from what we hear at {TOWN}.
[us] {OFFICER} wouldn't know what to do otherwise.
[them] You're the {OFFICE}, aren't you?
[us] For my sins, yes.
[them,their:lowtech] Then you are the one we deal with, and I'll tell them I met you.
[them] Then I'll know who to complain to.
[them] Your elders send their errands to ours more often than the moons turn.
[us] We have a lot to say to each other, it seems.
[them] Your {OFFICE} has a good hand for letters, for someone without a title.
[us] I'll tell {OFFICER} you said so, the first part anyway.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s messages arrive on schedule, which is more than ours manage.
[us] {OFFICER} likes a schedule.
